title: Capture coherent selected operational backups
statement: The Work records Module shall capture coherent selected operational backups through its typed maintenance boundary, preserving actual scope, source meaning and safe failure.

what.problem: Copying only records, or capturing changing records and artifacts at different states, can produce a backup that cannot restore its claimed scope.
what.desired_outcome: A participant can distinguish a complete recoverable capture from an incomplete attempt and know which work it preserves.

why.rationale: SR-074 requires operational preservation; MOD-011 owns the associated store and maintenance activation, while MOD-010 owns admission and result presentation.

stakeholders: Project maintainers and authorized agents relying on retained operational work

conditions: An actor explicitly selects the supported maintenance task, scope, source expectations and destination.

contexts: MOD-011 through IF-003, invoked by MOD-010 through IF-004; engineering definitions remain repository-owned.

how.approach: Use the reviewed MOD-011 maintenance contract: coherent staged scope, explicit project/schema/integrity checks, exclusive activation and attributable recovery outcomes.

how_much.scope: Selected retained supported records and payloads only; no silent merge, universal history retention, source deletion or renewed engineering approval.

acceptance_criteria: For a selected project state containing Changes, findings and retained artifacts, a complete backup identifies the captured state, project, interpretation version, included records and artifacts, and declared exclusions; all included references resolve within the retained scope or are explicitly external.

When recording continues during capture, the backup represents one coherent declared state or reports that capture could not complete; it never combines incompatible record and artifact versions as a complete backup.
If a required artifact is missing, unreadable or fails its recorded integrity check, backup creation reports the affected scope and does not declare a complete backup.
Interruption, cancellation or insufficient destination capacity leaves existing valid backups and source work unchanged and identifies any incomplete output as unusable for complete restoration.
An explicitly selected narrower scope identifies exclusions and cannot claim to preserve excluded evidence, post-capture work or unsaved content.
The public maintenance contract identifies preview versus execution, current expectations and actual effects; interrupted activation remains fenced until explicitly reconciled.
assumptions: Required retained source material and supported interpretation information are accessible; failure of that premise is reported explicitly.
constraints: Historical subject/revision provenance remains stable; restoring operational state creates a fresh store incarnation so old mutation tokens cannot be replayed.

sources.basis: Reconcile the existing reviewed maintenance responsibility with explicit REM allocation. This allocation is design intent, not execution or satisfaction evidence.
